statement: For linear pUC19 (2686 bp), POST /primers/restriction_sites reports, for every curated panel enzyme that cuts, exactly the 0-based start indices at which that enzyme's REBASE recognition sequence occurs in the template, and reports no entry for an enzyme with no occurrence.

parameters.coordinates: 0-based index of the first base of the recognition sequence

statement: Every recognition sequence in the app's curated enzyme panel is its own IUPAC reverse complement, so a top-strand-only scan is complete for the panel; correspondingly, running the app's site finder on the reverse complement of pUC19 must return the mirror-image start indices 2686 - (start + size) of the forward-strand result.

The site finder must locate recognition sites that occur on the bottom strand: for the non-palindromic enzyme BsaI (site GGTCTC), whose recognition sequence occurs in pUC19 only on the bottom strand (its reverse complement GAGACC occurs on the top strand at 0-based 1765), /primers/restriction_sites must report exactly one site and /primers/digest must report exactly one cut, at 0-based 1760, so that the two endpoints agree on the number of sites.

parameters.note: BsaI is not in the shipped panel; the test adds it to the panel dicts the endpoints read, exercising the app's own search code with a non-palindromic recognition sequence. The defect it probes is latent for today's all-palindromic panel (see RE-2).

statement: A recognition site that spans the origin of a circular template is found exactly once, at its true start index near the end of the template, and produces exactly one cut; the same template analysed as linear finds no site at all.

parameters.template: pUC19 rotated left by 398 bases: puc19[398:] + puc19[:398]
parameters.site_spans: the last 3 bases (GAA) plus the first 3 bases (TTC) of the rotated template

statement: For a LINEAR template, n distinct cut positions yield n+1 fragments (excluding a zero-length end piece when a cut falls on a terminus), the fragment lengths sum to the template length, each fragment sequence equals the template slice between its boundaries, and the multiset of fragment lengths equals Biopython's catalyse(linear=True).

statement: For a CIRCULAR template, n distinct cut positions yield exactly n fragments (not n+1) — the last cut bridges the origin back to the first — the fragment lengths sum to the circle length, the origin-spanning fragment's sequence equals template[start:] + template[:end], and the multiset of fragment lengths equals Biopython's catalyse(linear=False).

statement: An enzyme with no recognition site in the template is reported as cutting zero times: it is absent from the /primers/restriction_sites result, and /primers/digest returns zero cut positions and exactly one fragment whose sequence is the whole template, for both linear and circular topology.

Overlapping recognition sites are each reported once: two ClaI sites that share two bases in AAATCGATCGATTTT are both found (starts 2 and 6, cuts 4 and 8, fragment lengths 4/4/7), and in pUC19 the mutually overlapping KpnI (407-412), SmaI (411-416) and AvaI (411-416) sites are all reported with their own cut positions.

IUPAC-ambiguous recognition sequences are expanded per ambiguous_dna_values: AvaI (CYCGRG) matches all four resolutions and AvaII (GGWCC) both, at the positions where they literally occur, and the cut_pattern the app reports for each enzyme is that enzyme's REBASE site string.

A template supplied with the layout characters that Biopython's FormattedSeq removes before searching (all whitespace and all digits) must be analysed as the biological sequence those characters interleave: for a GenBank-ORIGIN-style paste of pUC19, template_length is 2686, the EcoRI site is at 395, the cut is at 396, the fragment lengths are 396 and 2290, and every reported fragment sequence contains only nucleotide letters.

parameters.template: pUC19 as a GenBank ORIGIN block: 60 bases per line, lowercase, in space-separated blocks of 10, each line prefixed by its right-aligned 1-based start coordinate
parameters.crlf_variant: pUC19 wrapped at 60 columns with CRLF line endings; same expected values

statement: The two endpoints must describe the same molecule in the same coordinate system for the same request body: for any template and enzyme, the number of sites from /primers/restriction_sites equals the number of cuts from /primers/digest, and every reported cut equals a reported site start plus that enzyme's fst5 offset.

parameters.coherence_rule: cut_position == site_start + fst5 (modulo template length when circular), and len(sites) == len(cut_positions)
parameters.holds_for: the clean 2686-base pUC19, linear and circular, across the whole panel

statement: A template containing a character outside the IUPAC nucleotide alphabet is not an analysable sequence — Biopython refuses it with TypeError('Invalid character found in ...') — so both endpoints must reject it the way the app already rejects an unknown enzyme name, with an HTTP 4xx, rather than /primers/digest returning HTTP 500 from an unhandled TypeError while /primers/restriction_sites returns HTTP 200 with positions counted over the raw string.

statement: The digest report must not depend on the order of the enzymes in the request: AvaI (C^YCGRG, 5' overhang, ovhg -4) and KpnI (G_GTAC^C, 3' overhang, ovhg +4) both cut pUC19 at the same 0-based top-strand position 412, and digest(['AvaI','KpnI']) must return the same fragments — boundaries, lengths and end chemistry — as digest(['KpnI','AvaI']).

parameters.requirement: order-independent result; the two enzyme orders must produce identical DigestResult payloads
